title: [Bug] Qwen3.5 greedy outputs differ A LOT between v0.5.12 and v0.5.17.dev for the same multimodal request; v0.5.17.dev36 not self-consistent behind router
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are included below.

## Describe the bug

We serve the same VLM (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) with two SGLang builds on identical
hardware (NVIDIA H20, TP=1, 4 independent workers behind the SGLang router):

- Build A: **v0.5.12** (commit `5a15cde858ea09b77`)
- Build B: **v0.5.17.dev36+gcb05a44** (commit `cb05a44`)

Sending a **byte-identical** multimodal request (`prompt_tokens` = 3932 on both
builds) with `temperature=0`:

### 1. A and B produce substantially different outputs

The fork always happens in the same region — right after the shared prefix
`"... This is exactly what I need(ed)"` (output char ~149–162) — and the
continuations then diverge completely:

| | completion tokens | stable across repeats? |
|---|---|---|
| A (0.5.12) | 246 | yes, bit-stable |
| B (0.5.17.dev36) | 342/342/342 in one session; 282/134/134 in a later session | **no** |

Cross-build text similarity: 0.28–0.58.

### 2. B is not self-consistent at temperature=0

Across repeated identical requests behind the router, B returned 342/342/342
completion tokens in one session but 282/134/134 in a later one (see
`results/repro_verify.log` in the attachment). A is bit-stable across all
repeats. The router round-robins over 4 identical workers, so this points at
worker-level non-determinism at temperature=0 on v0.5.17.dev.

### 3. The divergence is an argmax flip on a near-tie

With `logprobs=True`, at the first divergence position (right after
`"... This is exactly what I "`):

| Build | top-1 | top-2 | top-2 logprob gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5.12 | `need` (-0.7474) | `needed` (-0.7474) | **0.0** |
| 0.5.17.dev36 | `needed` (-0.6269) | `need` (-0.8769) | 0.25 |

Each build picks a different winner and the free-form `<think>` continuation
diverges completely. In a later session the flip lands one token later
(`' accomplish'` with gap 0.625 on A vs `' see'` with gap 0.125 on B).
`prompt_tokens` is identical (3932) on both builds, so tokenization / image
preprocessing are not the cause.

### Real-world impact: the flip changes grounded-action coordinates

We first hit this while serving an SFT checkpoint of the same model in a
GUI-agent (computer-use) setting. The model outputs `left_click` actions with
screen coordinates; at one step of a task ("remove vim from the favorites
bar"), the identical request produced **semantically different actions** on the
two builds:

| Build | model coordinate (normalized) | scaled click @1920x1080 | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5.12 | `[87, 95]` | (167, 102) — center of the "Remove from Favorites" context-menu item | menu item clicked → **task succeeds** |
| 0.5.17.dev36 | `[217, 91]` / `[164, 91]` (varies across repeats) | (417, 98) / (315, 98) — ~250px away, misses the menu entirely | clicks a wrong element → **task fails** |

The reference trajectory from which this request was replayed succeeded with
exactly 0.5.12's action. Across 8 repeated identical requests, v0.5.17.dev36
**never** produced the correct coordinate: the argmax flip landed on the
leading digit of the x-coordinate, and autoregressive conditioning then kept
the rest of the number consistently wrong.

So the divergence is not limited to free-form `<think>` text: when the flipped
token is part of a grounded action (a coordinate), it changes which UI element
gets clicked and flips task success/failure — which makes cross-build
evaluation results non-comparable for agent workloads.

## Reproduction

Repro package: **`sglang_issue_repro.zip`** (attached below)

[sglang_issue_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31462585/sglang_issue_repro.zip)

Contents:

- `request_step1.json` — the exact request payload (OpenAI
  `/v1/chat/completions` format: system + 1 history turn + current turn, 2
  base64 PNG screenshots, `temperature=0, top_p=0.9, max_tokens=2048`,
  `enable_thinking=True`)
- `repro_compare.py` — standalone repro script (only needs `openai>=1.x`);
  sends the request N times to each endpoint and reports self-consistency,
  cross-version similarity, first divergence position, and (with `--logprobs`)
  the top-2 logprob gap at the diverging token
- `results/observed_outputs.json` — captured outputs of the first experiment
  (3 repeats per build + per-token top-2 logprobs around the divergence)
- `results/repro_verify.log` — a later verification run (3 repeats per build)
  showing v0.5.17.dev failing self-consistency behind the router
- `server_args/` — verbatim `ServerArgs(...)` from a worker log of each build
  (host / model path scrubbed)

```bash
pip install openai
python repro_compare.py \
    --request request_step1.json \
    --endpoint-a http://<server-a>:30000/v1 \
    --endpoint-b http://<server-b>:30000/v1 \
    --label-a sglang-0.5.12 --label-b sglang-0.5.17.dev36 \
    --runs 3 --logprobs
```

Expected: identical `prompt_tokens` on both builds; outputs differ; first
divergence right after `"... This is exactly what I need(ed)"` with a top-2
logprob gap ≤ 0.25 at the diverging token.

## Environment

- SGLang builds: `0.5.12` (commit `5a15cde858ea09b77`) vs
  `0.5.17.dev36+gcb05a44` (commit `cb05a44`)
- Model: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (VL), bfloat16, `context_length=32768`
- Hardware: NVIDIA H20, one worker per GPU, 4 workers behind the SGLang router
- Both builds launched with the same effective core arguments:
  `attention_backend='fa3'`, `sampling_backend='flashinfer'`,
  `mem_fraction_static=0.9`, `max_running_requests=16`,
  `chunked_prefill_size=8192`, `schedule_policy='fcfs'`, `page_size=1`,
  TP=1, radix cache enabled, cuda graphs enabled
- Full `ServerArgs` for both builds: `server_args/` in the attachment

Differences in effective `ServerArgs` between the two builds (all other keys
identical):

| key | 0.5.12 | 0.5.17.dev36 | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disable_overlap_schedule` | `True` (auto-forced: *"Disabling overlap schedule since mamba no_buffer is not compatible with overlap schedule"*) | `False` | 0.5.17 switches `mamba_radix_cache_strategy` from `no_buffer` to `extra_buffer`, which re-enables the overlap scheduler |
| cuda graph config | decode-only graphs (`cuda_graph_max_bs=256`, `disable_piecewise_cuda_graph=True`) | `cuda_graph_config` with **prefill breakable cuda graph** enabled (`tc_compiler='eager'`) | prefill also runs inside captured graphs on 0.5.17.dev |

### Questions

1. Is cross-build numeric divergence of greedy (temperature=0) outputs expected
   given the scheduler / cuda-graph changes above?
2. For v0.5.17.dev, is the router-level non-self-consistency (different workers
   → different greedy outputs for the same request) a known limitation? Is
   there a recommended configuration to make each worker — and workers
   mutually — bit-stable (e.g. disabling prefill cuda graphs / the overlap
   scheduler, or `enable_deterministic_inference`)?
